wiki_links.section: Appendix 10: Connections to the PKB & Other Reports
wiki_links.context_line: > - **[[Cognitive-Load-Theory]]** — The liberation mechanism is a cognitive load claim: habitualization shifts behavioral control from the resource-intensive prefrontal system to the resource-efficient basal ganglia, directly reducing the intrinsic cognitive load of the routine and freeing working memory for higher-order processing. Without CLT's architecture, the PKB import of habit automaticity would be unclear.

wiki_links.section: Appendix 10: Connections to the PKB & Other Reports
wiki_links.context_line: > - **[[Memory-Systems]]** — Habit formation is a memory phenomenon: specifically, a shift from declarative encoding (how to perform the behavior, explicitly recalled) to procedural non-declarative encoding (the behavior executed without explicit recall). The multi-store memory architecture is the prerequisite for understanding why habitualized behaviors do not "tax" the same systems as novel behaviors.

wiki_links.section: Appendix 10: Connections to the PKB & Other Reports
wiki_links.context_line: > - **[[Self-Determination-Theory]]** — The motivational dimension of habit maintenance — why habits survive or decay — maps directly onto the SDT regulatory continuum. Habits built on external regulation are brittle; habits built on identified or integrated regulation are durable. SDT provides the motivational theory that explains long-term habit maintenance beyond the neurological account.

wiki_links.section: Appendix 10: Connections to the PKB & Other Reports
wiki_links.context_line: > - **[[Volitional-Congruence]]** — Understanding habit formation clarifies the volitional architecture: volitional strategies are most needed during the habit formation window; once the habit is established, volitional demand drops substantially. This means the PKB's work on volitional strategies should now be read as a theory of the formation phase, not the maintenance phase.

wiki_links.section: Appendix 10: Connections to the PKB & Other Reports
wiki_links.context_line: > - **[[Metacognition-&-Lifelong-Learning]]** — The claim that metacognitive expertise requires habitualized foundational procedures (reading, note-taking, self-questioning) is now grounded in specific mechanism: automatization of procedures frees metacognitive resources for genuine monitoring work. This enriches the lifelong learning node with a mechanistic explanation for why building learning habits is a prerequisite for deep metacognitive engagement.

wiki_links.section: Appendix 10: Connections to the PKB & Other Reports
wiki_links.context_line: > - **[[Self-Directed-Learning]]** — Self-direction requires the efficient execution of self-directed activities; efficient execution requires habitualization. This report provides the cognitive architecture explanation for why self-directed learners who have habitualized their learning routines can sustain more complex intellectual work than those for whom every study session requires renewed deliberation.

wiki_links.section: Appendix 10: Connections to the PKB & Other Reports
wiki_links.context_line: > - **[[Attribution-Theory]]** — Attribution patterns during the habit formation window are critical: learners who attribute early failures to strategy inadequacy (controllable, unstable) rather than ability (uncontrollable, stable) are more likely to persist through the effortful formation phase. Attribution theory enriches the practical account of habit resilience.

wiki_links.section: Appendix 10: Connections to the PKB & Other Reports
wiki_links.context_line: > - **[[Growth-Mindset]]** — The growth mindset framework is implicitly a theory about the habitualibility of competence: the belief that ability develops through practice is the belief that repeated effortful action can create automatic competence where none existed. Every habit formation success is evidence for the growth mindset ontology.

wiki_links.section: Appendix 10: Connections to the PKB & Other Reports
wiki_links.context_line: > - **[[Schema-Theory]]** — Schemas and habits both represent automatized cognitive structures encoding patterns that can be rapidly recognized and executed. The schema construction literature illuminates *cognitive* habituation (knowledge becomes schematic); the habit formation literature illuminates *behavioral* habituation. Together they describe the full arc from explicit learning to fluent performance.
